headline: Dhaka South City Corporation offers job opportunities in 9th and 10th grades
summary: A total of 18 positions are available in the revenue sector, with the application deadline set for November 26, 2026. Interested candidates can apply online.
details: Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) has published a recruitment notice for 9th and 10th grade positions in its revenue sector. A total of 18 posts are available for eligible candidates.
The application process commenced on November 5, 2026, at 10 AM. The final deadline for submitting applications and fees is November 26, 2026, by 5 PM.

The standard application fee is BDT 223. However, candidates from underprivileged groups, including minority ethnic communities, physically challenged individuals, and the third gender, are eligible for a reduced fee of BDT 56.

headline: South Korea targets 400,000 foreign students, offers 3-year post-study stay with new visa changes
summary: South Korea aims to attract 400,000 international students, introducing visa changes that prioritize Korean language proficiency and allow graduates to stay for up to three years after study.
details: South Korea has set a new ambitious target to attract 400,000 international students, having already surpassed its previous goal of 300,000 two years ahead of schedule by mid-2025. By February 2026, the number of foreign students reached 314,000.
To further boost international student numbers, the government is revising its student visa system. The proposed changes will place a greater emphasis on proficiency in the Korean language.

Under the new framework, most international students who can demonstrate intermediate Korean language skills will be exempt from providing proof of financial capability for their visa applications. This requires achieving Level 4 in the TOPIK exam or the Korean Immigration and Integration Program (KIIP).
However, students deemed at higher risk of overstaying their visas or prioritizing employment over studies may still be required to deposit funds to cover living expenses for a specified period.

The new structure also allows foreign graduates to stay in South Korea for one to three years after graduation, depending on their linguistic ability and job readiness. This aims to enhance their success in studies, adaptation to Korean society, and employment opportunities.
The government is also considering a new 'Korean Study Alumni Visitor Visa' to encourage international students to maintain ties with South Korea even after graduation.

While these changes may pose new challenges for students primarily seeking English-medium degrees or those drawn by Korean culture without strong language skills, opportunities still exist. Over 1,000 departments across more than 70 South Korean universities offer degree programs taught in English.
